name: Wakaway Global Logistics
tagline: From one okada to container ships. If e fit move, we go move am.

ownerCharacter.name: Oga Ifeanyi Waybill
ownerCharacter.look: Early 30s, lean. Orange reflective rider jacket over white shirt, navy trousers, scuffed boots, orange helmet under arm. Prop: fat waybill booklet and pen.
ownerCharacter.backstory: Lost his shop job, borrowed a second-hand motorbike from his uncle and started carrying parcels across Lagos. He never lost a package, so customers nicknamed him Waybill. Now he wants his name on a ship.

storyline.title: One Bike, One Phone
storyline.stage: A roadside umbrella stand in Yaba with one motorbike and a delivery box.
storyline.story: Ifeanyi collects parcels from online sellers and delivers them himself. Rain, traffic and a cracked phone screen fight him daily. If he loses one parcel, the sellers will go back to his rival. Every safe delivery builds his name.
storyline.unlock: Bike parcel line, the drop-off yard and the dispatch counter

storyline.title: The Rider Squad
storyline.stage: A small shop front with five bikes, a sorting shelf and a signboard.
storyline.story: Orders are more than one man can carry. Ifeanyi hires riders, buys helmets and insures the bikes. A rider who speeds can spoil the brand, so he trains them: safe first, fast second. Sellers start calling Wakaway by name.
storyline.unlock: Riders as staff, the sorting table and the Chief Rider

storyline.title: Waybill to Every State
storyline.stage: A courier office with two vans, a parcel cage and a weighing scale.
storyline.story: A fabric trader in Kano begs for next-day parcels. Ifeanyi opens an interstate waybill desk and sends vans up north. One van breaks down in Lokoja with 200 parcels inside. He must rescue the load before trust breaks.
storyline.unlock: Interstate waybill line, delivery vans and the first Kano trip

storyline.title: Big Wheels
storyline.stage: A truck park in Ogba with three 40-foot flatbeds and a diesel tank.
storyline.story: A factory owner offers a contract: move containers to Kano every week. The trucks cost more than everything Ifeanyi owns. He takes a bank loan from Harmattan Trust Bank. Now diesel prices and empty return trips decide if he sleeps.
storyline.unlock: Haulage line, trailer trucks, the loading bay and diesel costs

storyline.title: The Warehouse Years
storyline.stage: A fenced warehouse with racks, a forklift, loading bays and a gatehouse.
storyline.story: Customers want storage as well as transport. Ifeanyi builds a warehouse on the Lagos-Ibadan road. An auditor finds stock that does not match the books. He fixes the records, adds scanners, and wins a big supermarket contract.
storyline.unlock: Warehouse venue, the Parcel Belt machine and bulk contracts

storyline.title: Clearing Agent Licence
storyline.stage: A clearing and forwarding office beside Apapa port with a container yard.
storyline.story: Importers keep asking who can clear their goods. Ifeanyi sits the customs licence exam and opens at the port. A stranger offers a shortcut to skip inspection. He says no, declares every item properly, and becomes the agent people trust.
storyline.unlock: Container clearing line, customs paperwork desk and the demurrage clock

storyline.title: Borders and Hubs
storyline.stage: A regional group: Lagos head office, Cotonou depot, Durban and Dubai desks.
storyline.story: Cargo is jumping to Cotonou and Wakaway must follow it. Ifeanyi opens hubs abroad and learns new rules in each one. A late shipment in Durban threatens his biggest client. He flies out himself to sort it and saves the account.
storyline.unlock: Branches abroad, international flights and the Gantry Crane

storyline.title: MV Waybill Sails
storyline.stage: A shipping line with container ships and offices on four continents.
storyline.story: Ifeanyi charters his first container ship from Guangzhou to Lagos, then buys it. Freight rates swing wildly and one bad season could sink the line. The ship docks at Tin Can with his nickname on the hull, and his uncle cuts the ribbon.
storyline.unlock: Ocean freight line, own ships, and Rotterdam and Guangzhou offices

howItFitsTheEngine: The player carries parcels from the customer drop-off yard, and later containers from a ship at the quay (by trolley, then forklift), to stations: sorting table, weighing scale, customs paperwork desk and loading bay. Processed loads go to the dispatch counter, where riders, trucks and customers collect them and pay. Venues grow from umbrella stand to shop, depot, warehouse and port terminal.

staffRoles.does: Takes sorted parcels from the dispatch counter and delivers them round the city.
staffRoles.look: Young, slim, orange helmet and reflective vest, knee guards, delivery box on a red motorbike.

staffRoles.does: Sorts, labels and weighs parcels at the sorting table.
staffRoles.look: Woman in navy polo and orange apron, hair in a bun, label gun in hand, marker behind her ear.

staffRoles.does: Drives loaded trailers from the loading bay to other states and back.
staffRoles.look: Stocky man in his 40s, faded blue coverall, face cap, towel on shoulder, big bunch of keys.

staffRoles.does: Helps the driver, checks tyres and locks, and guards the load on the road.
staffRoles.look: Wiry man of 20, grey singlet under open orange vest, wheel spanner in hand.

staffRoles.does: Moves pallets and containers between the yard, racks and loading bays.
staffRoles.look: Calm woman in yellow hard hat, green coverall and safety boots, seated on a yellow forklift.

staffRoles.does: Prepares customs documents and declares every container correctly.
staffRoles.look: Sharp man in white shirt and loosened tie, ID lanyard, thick file under arm, stamp in hand.

staffRoles.does: Tracks every bike, truck and ship and keeps the whole site running without you.
staffRoles.look: Tall woman in navy blazer over ankara top, tablet showing a map, headset, calm smile.

machines.name: Parcel Conveyor Belt
machines.does: Carries parcels from the drop-off yard to the sorting table by itself.
machines.look: Waist-high grey roller belt with orange side rails, small scanner arch and a blinking green light.

machines.name: Yard Forklift Team
machines.does: Automatic forklifts move containers from the paperwork desk to the loading bays.
machines.look: Two yellow forklifts with orange beacons, Wakaway logo on the side, following painted floor lines.

machines.name: Quay Gantry Crane
machines.does: Lifts containers off the ship and stacks them in the yard with no carrying.
machines.look: Huge blue and orange crane on rails over the quay, cabin at the top, cables lifting a red container.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Hired riders keep 70% of each N3,000 delivery fee. You keep N900 but riders deliver while you do other things. Deliver it yourself and you keep the full fee.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Lagos couriers typically take around 60 to 75 percent of the delivery fee; the platform or company keeps the rest.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: A N3.2m Lagos to Kano trip costs about 45% in diesel, tolls and driver allowance. A daily diesel price can swing this from 40% to 55%. A better truck cuts it by 5%.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Fuel is the biggest cost in Nigerian haulage, and energy price rises have pushed interstate container rates up sharply.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: A truck coming back empty earns N0. Find a return load in Kano (grains, hides or textiles) and the trip earns an extra 50%, about N1.6m.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Hauliers hunt for backhaul cargo because an empty return leg doubles the real cost of a trip.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Each container has 3 free days at the quay. After that the customer is charged N40,000 a day and your trust rating drops 2 points daily until it is cleared.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Terminals and shipping lines give a few free days, then charge daily storage and demurrage on uncleared containers.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Customers give you duty money with the job. It sits in a locked pot and goes to customs in full. Your income is only the N250,000 fee. Wrong declarations are fined N500,000.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Clearing agents pay duty on behalf of importers and earn an agency fee; false declaration attracts penalties and seizure.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Ocean freight is quoted at $5,067 per 40ft. The naira value changes daily by up to 5% with the exchange rate, and by season: up 20% before Christmas.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Shipping lines quote freight in US dollars and rates rise in peak season, so naira earnings move with the exchange rate.

travel.why: Visit the port yard to check that containers are cleared before the demurrage clock runs out.
Inspect the border depot and handle cargo that importers have routed through the Cotonou port.
Meet northern traders, inspect the truck depot and find return loads so trailers never come back empty.
Sign export contracts for cocoa and sesame and inspect the European office.
Book ship space, meet factory suppliers and watch Wakaway containers get loaded at the port.

events.name: Detty December Rush
events.text: Everybody is sending gifts. Parcel orders double for today.

events.name: Third Mainland Go-Slow
events.text: Heavy traffic on the bridge. Bike deliveries take twice as long today.

events.name: Diesel Price Jump
events.text: Diesel is up again. Every haulage trip costs 10% more today.

events.name: Return Load Found
events.text: A Kano trader has grains for Lagos. Your truck earns on the way back.

events.name: Rainy Day Parcels
events.text: Heavy rain. Wrap parcels in nylon or pay for two soaked cartons.

events.name: Five-Star Review
events.text: A big online seller praises Wakaway. New customers arrive all day.

events.name: Port System Down
events.text: The customs portal is offline. Paperwork desks are slow until evening.

events.name: Naira Gains Today
events.text: The exchange rate moved your way. Ocean freight earns 5% more today.

endgame: Wakaway Lines owns a fleet of container ships and offices in Lagos, Cotonou, Durban, Rotterdam, Dubai and Guangzhou. Ifeanyi sits on the national shippers' council, runs a rider training school, and MV Waybill is the pride of Tin Can quay.
risksToHandleCarefully: Port bribery, smuggling and false declaration must only appear as offers the player refuses or errors to fix. Show riders with helmets and safe riding, never reward speeding. No child staff. Exchange-rate swings must not feel like gambling.

research.claim: Lagos last-mile delivery in 2026 costs roughly N1,500 to N4,000 by zone and N8,000 to N12,000 for long-haul parcels, with couriers taking about 60 to 75 percent of the fee.
In February 2023 hauling a 40-foot container from the Lagos ports to Kano, Kaduna, Abuja or Onitsha cost N1.8 million to N2.3 million, up from about N1.2 million.
A May 2026 breakdown of Apapa export costs lists freight forwarding at N200,000 to N250,000 and terminal handling at N100,000 to N120,000 per 20-foot container.
Ocean freight for a 40-foot container from north China to Apapa was quoted at about $5,067 in May 2026, with 35 to 48 days port to port from South China.
In May 2026 an importers' association official said clearing through Lagos costs about N3 million to N4 million more per container than Cotonou, pushing cargo there.
A 2026 wage survey puts most Nigerian heavy truck drivers at about N24,000 to N65,000 a month base pay, so the game pays above this with trip allowances included.
